mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real discount rates and drives up equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite FEDFUNDS up move; or the inflation surprise index (CPIAUCSL) falls sharply within the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months signals accommodative policy, lowering borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite, which tends to lift S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month's value for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in all three months of easing; or industrial production (INDPRO) shows no acceleration during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests a tight labor market, which can boost corporate profits and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal; or the ratio of PAYEMS/UNRATE does not exceed 2.5x in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand indicators HOUST (retail sales) exceed 2% above the prior month's level while industrial production INDPRO remains flat, it signals a shift toward services-driven growth, which is associated with higher S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% while INDPRO remains unchanged in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or indistinguishable from baseline in such episodes; or the ratio of HOUST to INDPRO does not exceed 1.5x.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in a month, without a corresponding drop in HOUST (retail sales), suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% while HOUST increases or remains flat in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the supply contraction; or the ratio of HOUST/INDPRO does not fall below 0.7 in such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 4.5% followed by a sustained drop below 4.0% over the next two months indicates a policy shift toward job creation, which typically supports equity valuations and yields a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for two consecutive months then UNRATE < 4.0% in the following two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative during the recovery phase; or GDP growth (not modeled here) is negative during the recovery.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI index) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.4% in a month, it suggests inflationary pressures that the Fed may respond to with higher rates, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.4% in a month with no prior warning
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the CPI surprise; or FEDFUNDS does not rise in response within the same quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in both INDPRO (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 8% over three consecutive months indicates a dual supply shock, which tends to reduce corporate earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month's value for three months and RSAFS < previous month's value for the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in all three months of contraction; or the ratio of INDPRO/RSAFS does not fall below 1.2 during the period.
